factProposals.value: Outside systems can create, update and complete work orders over a documented HTTP API (/api/v1/work-orders) with the work_orders:write scope; changes are audited as '<actor> via <system>' and pushed to GIS. Exercised with a simulated external system.
Work orders carry a version number, increased on every change (update, complete, GIS change, publish); api_request_log records every HTTP request.
An outside system working from a stale copy is refused with 412 and given the current work order, rather than overwriting another change.
Every API request is logged with time, client, IP, status and the body's field names; body values and API keys are never stored. Write access needs its own scope; read-only clients get 403.

Which vendors will connect, what their systems need from the API, and whether they accept this contract, ETag/If-Match and Idempotency-Key are not known; REQ-054's vendor coordination has not happened.

decisions.statement: Use ETag / If-Match with a per-work-order version for outside writes, returning 412 on a stale version and 428 when missing.
decisions.rationale: Prevents lost updates between outside systems and city staff; using headers kept the published JSON format unchanged.

decisions.statement: Scope Idempotency-Key to the calling system.
decisions.rationale: Retries are safe, and two systems choosing the same key cannot see or overwrite each other's work order.

decisions.statement: Log every request centrally at the top of the server, storing body field names and sizes but not values.
decisions.rationale: No endpoint can skip the log, and personal data in bodies is not copied into it.

decisions.statement: Generate the OpenAPI request bodies from the same field lists the endpoints validate against.
decisions.rationale: The specification given to vendors is exactly what the API enforces.

limitations.statement: The specification has not been reviewed or tested by any vendor yet (REQ-054).
The response format check before sending is a safety net that no test triggers, because the API's own output is always valid.
If the database is down, the request log row cannot be written; the failure is reported on the console only.
A repeated Idempotency-Key with a different body returns the first work order without flagging the difference.
The request log has no retention or clean-up yet, and it stores client IPs.
